*The LDA classifier therefore predicts class 1 if and only if *x* · *v* ⩽ α, where*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0074" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0034.gif"><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>-</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0034.gif)

*and*

*That is, the LDA classifier predicts class 1 if and only if *x* is on one side of the hyperplane*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0076" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0036.gif"><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>&#x2208;</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msup><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mo>:</mo><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>z</mi><mo>&#x00b7;</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>&#x03b1;</mi><mo>}</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0036.gif)

*When* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0017.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0017.gif)*and* L(1, 2) = L(2, 1), *the logarithmic term is zero and*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0077" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0037.gif"><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="true"><mrow><mi>&#x03b1;</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>-</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub></mfenced><mo>.</mo></mrow></mstyle></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0037.gif)

*In the setting of Exercise 2.2,* Σ = 1 *and m* = 1 *(which means vector inner product is scalar multiplication), so the LDA classifier predicts class 1 if and only if*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0078" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0038.gif"><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="true"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>-</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x2264;</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>-</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mo form="prefix">log</mo><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mfenced><mo>.</mo></mrow></mstyle></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0038.gif)

*If* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0018.gif"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>-</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0018.gif), *the above condition is equivalent to*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0079" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0039.gif"><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="true"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#x2264;</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>-</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mo form="prefix">log</mo><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mfenced><mo>,</mo></mrow></mstyle></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0039.gif)

*which is the solution of part D of Exercise 2.2 with* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0019.gif"><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0019.gif)*and* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0020.gif"><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0020.gif)*substituted for μ*[1] and *μ*[2].

In the case of binary classification with 0–1 loss and uniform class prior probabilities* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0021.gif"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0021.gif), *quadratic discriminant analysis predicts class 1 if and only if*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0111" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0040.gif"><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>&#x03c0;</mi></mrow><msub><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msup><mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><msubsup><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>&#x2265;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>|</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>&#x03c0;</mi><msub><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><msubsup><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0040.gif)

*or equivalently (taking logs of both sides and moving terms), if and only if*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0112" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0041.gif"><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><msubsup><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>-</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><msubsup><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>&#x2265;</mo><mo form="prefix">log</mo><mo>|</mo></mrow><msub><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo>|</mo><mo>-</mo><mo form="prefix">log</mo><mo>|</mo></mrow><msub><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo>|</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0041.gif)

*If we add the restrictions that μ*[1] = *μ*[2] *and Σ*[1] = *αΣ*[2] *for some α* > 1, *which appear to be approximately valid in the data illustrated in [Figure 4.31](#c04.xhtml#figure4-31), then quadratic discriminant analysis predicts class 1 if and only if*

*If β* = 0 *then all terms with k*[*m* + 1] > 0 *are zero, so the index set runs over all* (*k*[1], …, *k[m]*) ⩾ 0 *such that k*[1] + ⋅⋅⋅ + *k[m]* = *δ*.

Similarly, in the second term, where the random variable* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0022.gif"><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>-</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0022.gif)does not depend on *S* or *Y*. In the third term, the random variable <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0023.gif"><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>-</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0023.gif)*does not depend on *Y*, so the third term may be written as*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0126" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0048.gif"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>-</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi>X</mi></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>-</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi>X</mi></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mi> Var </mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0048.gif)

*(the first equality used the fact that *X* is independent of *S*). The fourth and fifth terms both involve random variables of the form (*Y* − *f*(*X*))*g*(*X*) for some function *g*. These two terms are both equal to zero: since E\[*Y* | *X*\] = *f*(*X*),*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0127" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0049.gif"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi>X</mi></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mo>|</mo><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>X</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0049.gif)

*The sixth term is shown to be zero in a similar way. It is the expected value of a random variable which does not depend on *Y*, and since *X* is independent of *S*,*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0128" type="mathematics"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0050.gif"><mtable displaystyle="true"><mtr><mtd/><mtd/><mtd columnalign="left"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>-</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>-</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd/><mtd/><mtd columnalign="left"><mrow><mspace width="2.em"/><mo>=</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi>X</mi></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>-</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>-</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0050.gif)

**Exercise 6.1** *Under squared-error loss, the risk is the squared bias of Z for θ plus the variance of *Z*. Since *c*[1] + ⋅⋅⋅ + *c[L]* =* 1,

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0153" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0051.gif"><mrow><mi> Bias </mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></munderover><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi> Bias </mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>&#x03b2;</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0051.gif)

*and since *Z*[1], …, *Z[L]* are uncorrelated,*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0154" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0052.gif"><mrow><mi> Var </mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></munderover><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi> Var </mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></munderover><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msubsup><mi>&#x03c3;</mi><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0052.gif)

*Thus minimizing the risk means minimizing*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0155" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0053.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>&#x03b2;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></munderover><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msubsup><mi>&#x03c3;</mi><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0053.gif)

*subject to the constraint *c*[1] + ⋅⋅⋅ + *c[L]* = 1. The Lagrangian for this constrained optimization problem is*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0156" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0054.gif"><mrow><msup><mi>&#x03b2;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></munderover><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msubsup><mi>&#x03c3;</mi><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></munderover><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mfenced><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0054.gif)

*Differentiating with respect to *c[l]* and setting the derivative equal to zero yields*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0157" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0055.gif"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msubsup><mi>&#x03c3;</mi><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>-</mo><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0055.gif)

*That is, at the critical point*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0158" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0056.gif"><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="true"><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msubsup><mi>&#x03c3;</mi><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mfrac><mo>&#x221d;</mo><msubsup><mi>&#x03c3;</mi><mi>l</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>.</mo></mrow></mstyle></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0056.gif)

*Using the fact that c*[1] + ⋅⋅⋅ + *c[L]* = 1,

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0159" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0057.gif"><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="true"><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msubsup><mi>&#x03c3;</mi><mi>l</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><msubsup><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>&#x03c3;</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mfrac><mo>.</mo></mrow></mstyle></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0057.gif)

*Since risk R grows without bound as any c[l] goes to ∞, R has no maximum. Since R ≥β, R has a minimum, and the critical point is the minimum. The minimum risk is*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0160" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0058.gif"><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="true"><mrow><msup><mi>&#x03b2;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></munderover><msup><mfenced open="(" close=")"><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msubsup><mi>&#x03c3;</mi><mi>l</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><msubsup><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>&#x03c3;</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msup><msubsup><mi>&#x03c3;</mi><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>&#x03b2;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mfenced open="(" close=")"><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msubsup><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>&#x03c3;</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.166667em"/><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></munderover><msubsup><mi>&#x03c3;</mi><mi>l</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>&#x03b2;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msubsup><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>&#x03c3;</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mfrac><mo>.</mo></mrow></mstyle></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0058.gif)

**Exercise 6.5** *Recall the notation of classification trees from [Section 4.8](#c04.xhtml#c4_8): *n[c]* is the number of training data of class *c* and *n^t[c]* is the number of training data of class *c* which enter node *t*. At leaf node *t*, a classification tree applies Bayes’ theorem*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0162" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0059.gif"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mo>|</mo><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>X</mi><mo>&#x2208;</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x221d;</mo><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>&#x2208;</mo><mi>t</mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mo>|</mo><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0059.gif)

*and uses the estimate*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0163" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0060.gif"><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="true"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>&#x2208;</mo><mi>t</mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mo>|</mo><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msubsup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mi>t</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mfrac><mo>.</mo></mrow></mstyle></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0060.gif)

*Node *t* classifies all data which enter it as the class *c* which minimizes the estimated posterior risk,*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0164" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0061.gif"><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="true"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>c</mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mo>|</mo><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>X</mi><mo>&#x2208;</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>C</mi></munderover><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mo>|</mo><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>X</mi><mo>&#x2208;</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x221d;</mo><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>C</mi></munderover><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mfrac><msubsup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow><mi>t</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow></mstyle></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0061.gif)

*Now suppose a tree is grown until all leaf nodes have zero impurity, and let t be a leaf node of this tree. *Thus leaf node *t* predicts class *c*′ regardless of the values taken by the loss function and regardless of the prior distribution on classes.*

**Exercise 7.1** *For any* *d*, 0 ⩽ *d* < *n* − 1, *approximation* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0025.gif"><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>d</mi></msub></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0025.gif)*is found by solving the optimization problem*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0167" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0064.gif"><mrow><mtable><mtr><mtd><mi> minimize </mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x2208;</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><msup><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>-</mo><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>d</mi></munderover><msub><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></msubsup></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0064.gif)

*and approximation* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0026.gif"><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0026.gif)*is found by solving the optimization problem*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0168" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0065.gif"><mrow><mtable><mtr><mtd><mi> minimize </mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x2208;</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><msup><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>-</mo><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><msub><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></msubsup></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0065.gif)

*Since any vector (θ*[0], *θ[1]*, …, *θ*[*d*]) *considered in the upper problem corresponds to a vector (θ*[0], θ[1], …, θ[*d*], 0) *considered in the lower problem, the solution to the lower problem is at least as good as the solution to the upper problem, that is*, <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0027.gif"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi> train </mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x2264;</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi> train </mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>d</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0027.gif). *If* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0028.gif"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi> train </mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>d</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0028.gif)*then* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0029.gif"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0029.gif)*in the solution of the lower problem since the solutions to these optimization problems are unique (by Exercise 3.2). The event* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0030.gif"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0030.gif)*has probability zero since* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0031.gif"><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0031.gif)*is Gaussian-distributed (as we saw in [Section 3.6](#c03.xhtml#c3_6)). When d* ⩾ *n* − 1, *there are enough parameters (θ*[0], θ[1], …, θ[*d*]*) to interpolate the points (x*[1], *y*[1]*), …, (*x[n]*, *y[n]*), at which point* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0032.gif"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi> train </mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>d</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0032.gif). *Specifically, when d* ⩾ *n* − 1, *any parameter vector (θ*[0], *θ*[1], …, *θ*[*d*]*) which solves the system of equations*

![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0066.gif)

produces an approximation <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0033.gif"><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>d</mi></msub></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0033.gif)with zero training risk (since the *x[i]*’s are distinct, the rows of the matrix are independent, and the system is solvable when *d* ⩾ *n* − 1). In terms of bias and variance, as *d* increases, the bias of <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0034.gif"><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>d</mi></msub></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0034.gif)goes down and the variance of <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0035.gif"><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>d</mi></msub></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0035.gif)goes up. Selecting a model based on the criterion of minimizing training risk will tend to result in selecting an overfit model.

**Exercise 7.5** *By Exercise 7.3,*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0174" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0067.gif"><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="true"><mrow><mi> Var </mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi> valid </mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mover accent="true"><mi>n</mi><mo>&#x02dc;</mo></mover></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow></mstyle></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0067.gif)

*As a function of* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0036.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0036.gif), *this increases from zero up to a unique maximum at* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0037.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0037.gif), *and then decreases.*

1.  *We choose* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0038.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>n</mi><mo>&#x02dc;</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0038.gif)*as small as possible so that* <displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0175" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0068.gif"><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="true"><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mover accent="true"><mi>n</mi><mo>&#x02dc;</mo></mover></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>&#x03c1;</mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><mi>&#x03c1;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x2264;</mo><msup><mi>&#x03c3;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo></mrow></mstyle></math></displayedItem>
    
    ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0068.gif)
    
    *so <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0039.gif"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>n</mi><mo>&#x02dc;</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>&#x2308;</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>&#x03c1;</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><mi>&#x03c1;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>&#x03c3;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>&#x2309;</mo></mrow></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0039.gif).*
    
2.  *This is (A) with the ρ chosen to maximize the upper bound on the variance, that is,* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0040.gif"><mrow><mi>&#x03c1;</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0040.gif). *This gives* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0041.gif"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>n</mi><mo>&#x02dc;</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>&#x2308;</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>&#x03c3;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>&#x2309;</mo></mrow></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0041.gif).
3.  <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0042.gif"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>n</mi><mo>&#x02dc;</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>1875</mn></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0042.gif).
4.  *The desired value for σ is unattainable unless* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0043.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0043.gif)*turns out to be considerably smaller than upper bound provided (ρ = 0.25)—a situation we would be unlikely to recognize without using much of the available data for validation. In case (D), either much more than 1800 data are needed, or the target upper bound for the standard deviation (σ = 0.01) must be relaxed.*

**Exercise ^(10.4)** *The halting criterion is as follows. Having proposed the parameter value θ*[*i* + 1], *apply the level-α one-sided Z*\-*test developed in part (C) of Exercise 7.5 to test the null hypothesis* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0044.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msub><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x2265;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msub><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0044.gif)*against the alternative hypothesis* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0045.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msub><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msub><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0045.gif). *If this test retains the null hypothesis, halt and report θ[*i*] as an optimal value. If this test rejects the null hypothesis, continue the optimization. If it is known in advance that at most *I* iterations will be performed, then applying Bonferroni correction is equivalent to performing level-*<math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0046.gif"><mfrac><mi>&#x03b1;</mi><mi>I</mi></mfrac></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0046.gif)*tests in the halting criterion.*

**Exercise 10.5** *Let α* = E\[*X*\]. *Since g is concave, there is a line through the point* (*α*, *g*(*α*)) *such that the curve parametrized by* (*y*, *g*(*y*)) *is always on or below the line. Let s be the slope of such a line, so*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0197" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0073.gif"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>&#x2264;</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03b1;</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>&#x03b1;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0073.gif)

*for all* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0047.gif"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>&#x2208;</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0047.gif). *Then*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0198" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0074.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mo>\[</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>\]</mo><mo>&#x2264;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mo>\[</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03b1;</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>&#x03b1;</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>\]</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03b1;</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mo>\[</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>\]</mo><mo>-</mo><mi>s</mi><mi>&#x03b1;</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mo>\[</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>\]</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0074.gif)

*If *g* is strictly concave, then*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0199" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0075.gif"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03b1;</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>&#x03b1;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0075.gif)

*except at the point *y* = α, so*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0200" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0076.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mo>\[</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>\]</mo><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mo>\[</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>\]</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0076.gif)

*unless* P(*X* = *α*) = 1.

**Exercise 10.6** *Let *X* be a random variable with density P*[0] *and let *Z* be a random variable with density P*[1]. *We observe that*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0201" type="mathematics"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0077.gif"><mtable displaystyle="true"><mtr><mtd columnalign="right"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mfenced separators="" open="\[" close="\]"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mfenced></mrow></mtd><mtd><mo>=</mo></mtd><mtd columnalign="left"><mrow><mo>&#x222b;</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mo>&#x222b;</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>:</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x2264;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0077.gif)

*with equality if and only if*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0202" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0078.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0078.gif)

*Now*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0203" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0079.gif"><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mfenced separators="" open="\[" close="\]"><mo form="prefix">log</mo><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mfenced></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mfenced separators="" open="\[" close="\]"><mo form="prefix">log</mo><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mfenced></mfenced><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0079.gif)

*and applying Jensen’s inequality to the random variable* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0048.gif"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0048.gif), *since log is strictly concave on the positive reals,*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0204" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0080.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mfenced separators="" open="\[" close="\]"><mo form="prefix">log</mo><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mfenced></mfenced><mo>&#x2264;</mo><mo form="prefix">log</mo><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mfenced separators="" open="\[" close="\]"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mfenced></mfenced><mo>&#x2264;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0080.gif)

*with equality if and only if* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0049.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0049.gif)*for some constant c and* P(*P*[0](*Z*) > 0) = 1. *The equality conditions imply that for any set S*, P(*X* ∈ *S*) = *c* P(*Z* ∈ *S*). *The particular case S* = {*x*: *P*[0](*x*) > 0} *has*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0205" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0081.gif"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>&#x2208;</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>&#x2208;</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0081.gif)

*so c* = 1. *Therefore*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0206" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0082.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mfenced separators="" open="\[" close="\]"><mo form="prefix">log</mo><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mfenced></mfenced><mo>&#x2265;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0082.gif)

*with equality if and only if* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0050.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0050.gif).

*The derivative with respect to w[j] is*
