*and setting this equal to zero and solving for w[j] yields the solution*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0212" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0086.gif"><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>|</mo><mo>{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>:</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>}</mo><mo>|</mo></mrow><mi>&#x03bb;</mi></mfrac><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0086.gif)

*Since*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0213" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0087.gif"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>J</mi></munderover><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>J</mi></munderover><mfrac><mrow><mo>|</mo><mo>{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>:</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>}</mo><mo>|</mo></mrow><mi>&#x03bb;</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>n</mi><mi>&#x03bb;</mi></mfrac><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0087.gif)

*it follows that λ* = *n and so for all j*, *the unique critical point for *w[j]* is*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0214" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0088.gif"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>w</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>|</mo><mo>{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>:</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>}</mo><mo>|</mo></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0088.gif)

*Maximization of the Lagrangian with respect to μ*[1], …, *μ*[*J*], *Σ*[1], …, *Σ*[*J*] *when z*[1], …, *z[n] are known is identical to maximizing the log-likelihood of the model used in the quadratic discriminant classifier: this was done in Exercise 4.5.*

**Exercise 11.2** *Since X is uniformly distributed in the unit ball*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0230" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0089.gif"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="true">{</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mo>:</mo><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>&#x2264;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="true">}</mo><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0089.gif)

*the density of X*[1] *at the point x*[1] *is equal to the* (*m* − 1)-*dimensional volume of the intersection of *B* with the hyperplane*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0231" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0090.gif"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>{</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mo>:</mo><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x00b7;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>}</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0090.gif)

*The intersection* *B*∩*H is empty* (*so the volume is zero*) *unless x*[1] ∈ \[ − 1, 1\], *in which case the intersection B*∩*H is an* (*m* − 1)-*dimensional ball centered at* (*x*[1], 0, …, 0) with radius <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0051.gif"><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></msqrt></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0051.gif). *Thus the density of X*[1] *at x*[1] *is*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0232" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0091.gif"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mi>m</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></msqrt></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>&#x03c0;</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mo stretchy="true">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><msup><mo stretchy="true">)</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup></mrow><mrow><mi>&#x0393;</mi><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mfenced></mrow></mfrac><mo>&#x221d;</mo><mo stretchy="true">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><msup><mo stretchy="true">)</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0091.gif)

*for x*[1] ∈ \[ − 1, 1\]. *The density of X*[1] *is symmetric about zero, so X*[1] *has the distribution of N* × |*X*[1]|, *where the sign N is uniformly distributed on the set { − 1, 1} and |*X*[1]| is a random variable supported on the interval \[0, 1\], independent of *N*. This implies that*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0233" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0092.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mspace width="2.em"/><mi> and </mi><mspace width="2.em"/><mi> Var </mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mo stretchy="true">\[</mo><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="true">\]</mo><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><msup><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mo stretchy="true">\[</mo><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="true">\]</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0092.gif)

*The distribution of X*²[1] *is obtained by*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0234" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0093.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo stretchy="true">(</mo><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>&#x2264;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="true">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>&#x2264;</mo><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo stretchy="true">)</mo><mo>&#x221d;</mo><msubsup><mo>&#x222b;</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></msubsup><mo stretchy="true">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><msup><mo stretchy="true">)</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mo>&#x222b;</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mi>x</mi></msubsup><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0093.gif)

*using the substitution* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0052.gif"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0052.gif)*in the last integral. From this we recognize that* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0053.gif"><mrow><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>&#x223c;</mo><mi> Beta </mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0053.gif), *and therefore*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0235" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0094.gif"><mrow><mi> Var </mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mo stretchy="true">\[</mo><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="true">\]</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0094.gif)

**Exercise 11.4** *Let *D* be the distance between the origin and a point uniformly distributed the unit ball centered at the origin. For r* ∈ \[0, 1\], *the density of *D* is proportional to the surface area of an m*\-*dimensional sphere of radius *r*,*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0237" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0095.gif"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>&#x03c0;</mi><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mi>m</mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mi>&#x0393;</mi><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mfenced></mrow></mfrac><mo>&#x221d;</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0095.gif)

*From this we recognize that D is distributed Beta*(*m*, 1). *For the squared distance,*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0238" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0096.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#x2264;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>&#x2264;</mo><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x221d;</mo><msubsup><mo>&#x222b;</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></msubsup><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mo>&#x222b;</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mi>x</mi></msubsup><msup><mi>u</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0096.gif)

*using the substitution* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0054.gif"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0054.gif)*in the last integral. From this, we recognize that* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0055.gif"><mrow><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#x223c;</mo><mi> Beta </mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0055.gif).

**Exercise 11.7** *The inner sphere is tangent to the radius-*<math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0056.gif"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0056.gif)*sphere centered at* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0057.gif"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0057.gif)*at the point* (*x*, *x*, …, *x*), *where x is the smaller of the two solutions to the equation*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0254" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0097.gif"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msup><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.166667em"/></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0097.gif)

*that is*, <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0058.gif"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mi>m</mi></msqrt></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0058.gif). *The radius of *S* is the distance from* (*x*, *x*, …, *x*) *to the origin, which is*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0255" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0098.gif"><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>m</mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msup><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mi>m</mi></msqrt></mrow></mfrac></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msqrt><mi>m</mi></msqrt><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0098.gif)

*This radius exceeds* 1 (*and so S contains a point outside C*) *for all m* ⩾ 10.

**Exercise 11.10** *Let* **1** *denote the *n*\-long column vector of all 1’s*. *Multiplication of* **X** *on the left by the *n* × *n* matrix of all 1’s,* **11**^T, *results in a matrix with constant columns, and each entry in the *i*th column of* **11**^T**X** *is the sum of all elements in the *i*th column of* **X**. *Thus each entry in the *i*th column of* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0059.gif"><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0059.gif)*is the mean of all elements in the *i*th column of* **X**, *so*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0262" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0099.gif"><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced separators="" open="\[" close="\]"><mtable><mtr><mtd><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>&#x203e;</mo></mover></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>&#x203e;</mo></mover></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mo>&#x22ee;</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>&#x203e;</mo></mover></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0099.gif)

*Therefore,*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0263" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0100.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mi mathvariant="bold">I</mi><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup></mfenced><mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi><mo>-</mo><mfenced separators="" open="\[" close="\]"><mtable><mtr><mtd><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>&#x203e;</mo></mover></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>&#x203e;</mo></mover></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mo>&#x22ee;</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>&#x203e;</mo></mover></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0100.gif)

*is the matrix formed by subtracting* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0060.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>&#x203e;</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0060.gif)*from each row of* **X**. *The idempotency of* **H** *could be said simply to follow from the above property, but formally it is shown by*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0264" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0101.gif"><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mi mathvariant="bold">I</mi><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">I</mi><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn></mrow><mo>&#x23df;</mo></munder><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></munder><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">I</mi><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0101.gif)

*The rows of* **HX** *are* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0061.gif"><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>-</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>&#x203e;</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>-</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>&#x203e;</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>-</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>&#x203e;</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0061.gif), *so*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0265" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0102.gif"><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>-</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>&#x203e;</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>-</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>&#x203e;</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">S</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0102.gif)

**Exercise 11.12** *Since **Q** is an orthogonal matrix, its columns are all mutually orthogonal unit vectors, so (1) is satisfied. For (2), let *z* be an arbitrary *m*\-dimensional unit vector. The sample variance of* **HX***z is, by Exercise 11.10,*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0267" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0103.gif"><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>z</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi></mfenced><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>z</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi mathvariant="bold">S</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>z</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#x039b;</mi></mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#x039b;</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0103.gif)

*Note that since *z* is a unit vector and* **Q** *is orthogonal,* **Q**^T*z is also a unit vector* (*because* ‖**Q**^T*z*‖² = *z*^T**QQ**^T*z* = *z*^T*z* = ‖*z*‖² = 1). *Since* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0062.gif"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#x039b;</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi> diag </mi><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0062.gif), *the last expression for the sample covariance of* **HX***z can be written as*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0268" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0104.gif"><mrow><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></munderover><msub><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>i</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0104.gif)

*Since λ*[1] ⩾ *λ*[2] ⩾ ⋅⋅⋅ ⩾ *λ*[*m*] ⩾ 0, *the above expression for the sample covariance of* **HX***z is maximized when *z* is chosen so that*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0269" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0105.gif"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced separators="" open="\[" close="\]"><mtable><mtr><mtd><mn>1</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mo>&#x22ee;</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0105.gif)

*or equivalently, multiplying on the left by* **Q**, *when*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0270" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0106.gif"><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mfenced separators="" open="\[" close="\]"><mtable><mtr><mtd><mn>1</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mo>&#x22ee;</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0106.gif)

*unless λ[1] = 0. But if λ[1] = 0 then for all *z*,*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0271" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0107.gif"><mrow><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></munderover><msub><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>i</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></munderover><mn>0</mn><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>i</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0107.gif)

*and we are free to choose z* = *Q*[1] *as the (non-unique) maximizer. For (3), suppose we have shown that (3) holds for all j* = 1, …, *h*. *We will show that (3) holds for j* = *h* + 1. *Let *z* be an arbitrary *m*\-dimensional unit vector, and observe that the sample covariance between* **HX***Q[j] and* **HX***z is*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0272" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0108.gif"><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi> as </mi><mspace width="4pt"/><mi> above </mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#x039b;</mi></mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi>z</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0108.gif)

*Since **Q** is orthogonal,*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0273" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0109.gif"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#x039b;</mi></mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>&#x23df;</mo></munder><mrow><mn>1</mn><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mrow><mi> in </mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi> position </mi></mrow><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>j</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#x039b;</mi></mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0109.gif)

*Thus if the sample covariance between* **HX***Q[j] and* **HX***z is zero for j* = 1, …, *h then*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0274" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0110.gif"><mrow><msub><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mspace width="2.em"/><mi> for </mi><mspace width="4pt"/><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0110.gif)

*As in (2), finding z which maximizes the sample variance of* **HX***z is equivalent to finding z which maximizes*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0275" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0111.gif"><mrow><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></munderover><msub><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>i</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0111.gif)

*and if the sample covariance between* **HX***Q[j] and* **HX***z is zero for j* = 1, …, *h then the expression to be maximized becomes*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0276" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0112.gif"><mrow><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></munderover><msub><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mspace width="0.166667em"/><msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>i</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0112.gif)

*The argument that z* = *Q*[*h* + 1] *maximizes this expression* (*whether λ*[*h* + 1] > 0 or *λ*[*h* + 1] = 0) *is the same as the argument for z* = *Q*[1] in (2).

**Exercise 11.15** *For part (A), let* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0063.gif"><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>&#x03bb;</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0063.gif)*and let* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0064.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>&#x02dc;</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0064.gif)*be a solution to the constrained optimization problem*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0283" type="mathematics"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0113.gif"><mtable displaystyle="true"><mtr><mtd columnalign="right"><mrow><mtext mathvariant="monospace">minimize</mtext><mspace width="4.pt"/><mtext mathvariant="monospace">over</mtext><mspace width="4.pt"/><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mtext>:</mtext></mrow></mtd><mtd/><mtd columnalign="left"><mrow><mspace width="1.em"/><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right"><mrow><mi mathvariant="monospace">subject</mi><mi mathvariant="monospace">to</mi><mo>:</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd/><mtd columnalign="left"><mrow><mspace width="1.em"/><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x2264;</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>&#x03bb;</mi></msub><mo>.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0113.gif)

*If* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0065.gif"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>&#x02dc;</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0065.gif)*then, since* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0066.gif"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>&#x02dc;</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x2264;</mo><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0066.gif), <displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0284" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0114.gif"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>&#x02dc;</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>&#x02dc;</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem>

![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0114.gif)

*contradicting the fact that* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0067.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0067.gif)*minimizes* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0068.gif"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0068.gif). So <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0069.gif"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>&#x02dc;</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x2265;</mo><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0069.gif), *that is*, <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0070.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0070.gif)*is a solution to the constrained problem. For part (B), let* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0071.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0071.gif)*be a solution to the constrained optimization problem* <displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0285" type="mathematics"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0115.gif"><mtable displaystyle="true"><mtr><mtd columnalign="right"><mrow><mtext mathvariant="monospace">minimize</mtext><mspace width="4.pt"/><mtext mathvariant="monospace">over</mtext><mspace width="4.pt"/><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mtext>:</mtext></mrow></mtd><mtd/><mtd columnalign="left"><mrow><mspace width="1.em"/><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right"><mrow><mi mathvariant="monospace">subject</mi><mi mathvariant="monospace">to</mi><mo>:</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd/><mtd columnalign="left"><mrow><mspace width="1.em"/><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>&#x2264;</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></math></displayedItem>

![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0115.gif)

*(if this constrained optimization problem has more than one solution, take* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0072.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0072.gif)*so that* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0073.gif"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0073.gif)*is as small as possible). If* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0074.gif"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0074.gif), *then* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0075.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0075.gif)*is a local minimum of *g*. Since *g* is convex,* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0076.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0076.gif)*is a global minimum of *g*, and therefore* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0077.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0077.gif)*is a solution to the unconstrained optimization problem*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0286" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0116.gif"><mrow><mtext mathvariant="monospace">minimize</mtext><mspace width="4.pt"/><mtext mathvariant="monospace">over</mtext><mspace width="4.pt"/><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mtext>:</mtext><mspace width="1.em"/><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0116.gif)

*for the value λ*[*c*] = 0. *If* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0078.gif"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0078.gif), *then* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0079.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0079.gif)*is a solution to the constrained optimization problem*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0287" type="mathematics"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0117.gif"><mtable displaystyle="true"><mtr><mtd columnalign="right"><mrow><mtext mathvariant="monospace">minimize</mtext><mspace width="4.pt"/><mtext mathvariant="monospace">over</mtext><mspace width="4.pt"/><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mtext>:</mtext></mrow></mtd><mtd/><mtd columnalign="left"><mrow><mspace width="1.em"/><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right"><mrow><mi mathvariant="monospace">subject</mi><mi mathvariant="monospace">to</mi><mo>:</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd/><mtd columnalign="left"><mrow><mspace width="1.em"/><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0117.gif)

*Let* ∂*H* = {*θ*: *h*(*θ*) = *c*} *be the boundary of the set H* = {*θ*: *h*(*θ*) ⩽ *c*}. *At every point θ* ∈ ∂*H*, *the gradient* ∇*h*(*θ*) *is orthogonal to ∂*H* and points outside of H* (*since h*(*θ*) *increases as θ moves from inside H* = {*θ*: *h*(*θ*) ⩽ *c*} *across the boundary* ∂*H* = {*θ*: *h*(*θ*) = *c*} *to the complement of H*, *which is* {*θ*: *h*(*θ*) > *c*}). *In particular*, <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0080.gif"><mrow><mi>&#x2207;</mi><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0080.gif)*is orthogonal to *H* at* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0081.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0081.gif). *Also*, <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0082.gif"><mrow><mi>&#x2207;</mi><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0082.gif)*is orthogonal to *H* at* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0083.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0083.gif), *because if it were not, then a small move within *H* would reduce the value of *g*, and* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0084.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0084.gif)*would not be a solution to the constrained optimization problem. That is, there is a scalar λ such that*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0288" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0118.gif"><mrow><mi>&#x2207;</mi><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>&#x2207;</mi><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0118.gif)

*Let* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0085.gif"><mrow><mi>&#x2202;</mi><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>{</mo><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>:</mo><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0085.gif)*be the boundary of the set* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0086.gif"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>{</mo><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>:</mo><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x2264;</mo><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0086.gif)(*G is also a convex set*). *At every point θ* ∈ *∂G*, *the gradient* ∇*g*(θ) *is orthogonal to ∂G and points outside of G. The interior of H and *G* have empty intersection, because if they did not, there would exist a point θ such that* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0087.gif"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0087.gif)*and h*(*θ*) < *c*, *and then* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0088.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0088.gif)*would not be a solution to the constrained optimization problem. Thus at* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0089.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0089.gif), *which is in both ∂H and ∂*G*, the gradients* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0090.gif"><mrow><mi>&#x2207;</mi><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0090.gif)*and* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0091.gif"><mrow><mi>&#x2207;</mi><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0091.gif)*point in opposite directions, that is, λ* < 0. *Let λ*[*c*] = −*λ*. *Then λ*[*c*] ⩾ 0 *and*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0289" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0119.gif"><mrow><mi>&#x2207;</mi><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>&#x2207;</mi><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0119.gif)

*Since λ*[*c*] ⩾ 0, *g*(*θ*) + *λ*[*c*]*h*(*θ*) *is a convex function. Since* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0092.gif"><mrow><mi>&#x2207;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><msub><mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>=</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0092.gif), <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0093.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0093.gif)*is a local, and hence global, minimum of g*(*θ*) + *λ*[*c*]*h*(*θ*). *That is,* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0094.gif"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#x03b8;</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0094.gif)*is a solution of the unconstrained optimization problem.*

*Putting the losses on one side yields*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0304c" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0122.gif"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03c4;</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>&#x03c4;</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0122.gif)

**Exercise 12.2** *Since *F* is a cumulative distribution function, lim[*s* → −∞]*F*(*s*) = 0 and lim[*s* → ∞]*F*(*s*) = 1, and since *F* is continuous and strictly increasing, it is a one-to-one (hence invertible) and onto map of ( − ∞, ∞) to (0, 1). For any *u* ∈ (0, 1),*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0304d" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0123.gif"><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>U</mi><mo>&#x2264;</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="4pt"/><mo>=</mo><mspace width="4pt"/><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x2264;</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>&#x2264;</mo><msup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="4pt"/><mo>=</mo><mspace width="4pt"/><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0123.gif)

Thus *U* is uniformly distributed on (0, 1). Nothing changes if <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0095.gif"><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>&#x2265;</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0095.gif)(that is, *U* = *F*(*S*) is still uniformly distributed on (0, 1)).

**Exercise 12.3** *By application of Exercise 12.2, the distribution of* (*U*[1], *U*[2]) = *h*(*S*[1], *S*[2]) *is uniform on* (0, 1) × (0, 1) *since each coordinate is uniformly distributed on* (0, 1) *and the two coordinates are independent. By definition of the uniform distribution, the area under the ROC curve is the probability that the point* (*U*[1], *U*[2]) *is under the ROC curve, and since h is one-to-one, this is the probability that h maps* (*S*[1], *S*[2]) *to a point under the ROC curve. Now h maps a point* (*s*[1], *s*[2]) *under the ROC curve if and only if the point* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0096.gif"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>&#x2265;</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&#x2265;</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0096.gif)*is below the point* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0097.gif"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>&#x2265;</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&#x2265;</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0097.gif), *that is, if and only if* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0098.gif"><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&#x2265;</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x2264;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&#x2265;</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0098.gif). *Since* <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp02\_ILM0099.gif"><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&#x2265;</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp02_ILM0099.gif)*is a strictly decreasing function of *s*, *h* maps a point* (*s*[1], *s*[2]) *under the ROC curve if and only if s*[2] ⩾ *s*[1]. *Thus*

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0304e" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0124.gif"><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="4.pt"/><mtext>is</mtext><mspace width="4.pt"/><mtext>under</mtext><mspace width="4.pt"/><mtext>the</mtext><mspace width="4.pt"/><mtext>ROC</mtext><mspace width="4.pt"/><mtext>curve</mtext><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&#x2265;</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0124.gif)

**Exercise 12.7** Let *E[i]* be the event that the *i*th test, out of the *T* − *T*[0] tests in which the null hypothesis is false, incorrectly rejects the null. By Boole’s inequality, the probability that at least one test incorrectly rejects the null is

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0304" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0125.gif"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>&#x222a;</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>&#x222a;</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#x2264;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.166667em"/><mi>s</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0125.gif)

*The solution to the equation p*(*s*) = *α*, for 0 < *α* < 1, is

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0305" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0126.gif"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>&#x03b1;</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0126.gif)

*The value of T*[0] *is unknown, but since p*(*s*) *is a decreasing function of T*[0], *the value of s obtained by replacing T*[0] *with zero*,

<displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp02-disp-0306" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp02\_M0127.gif"><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>&#x03b1;</mi><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem> ![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp02_M0127.gif)

*provides a computable value such that *p*(*s*[0]) ⩽ α.*

# C  
Converting Between Normal Parameters and Level-Curve Ellipsoids

Let *Z* be a *m*\-dimensional normal random variable with mean *μ* and covariance matrix Σ. The density function for *Z* is <displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp03-disp-0001" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp03\_M0001.gif"><mrow><mi>&#x03c6;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>&#x03c0;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><msup><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem>

![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp03_M0001.gif)

so the level curves of the density can be written as <displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp03-disp-0002" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp03\_M0002.gif"><mrow><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>:</mo><mi>&#x03c6;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfenced separators="" open="{" close="}"><mi>z</mi><mo>:</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><msup><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo form="prefix">log</mo><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mi>c</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>&#x03c0;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><msup><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup></mfenced></mfenced><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem>

![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp03_M0002.gif)

so level curves of *φ*(*z*) are level curves of (*z* − *μ*)^TΣ^(− 1)(*z* − *μ*).

By a well-known theorem,^([1](#p03.xhtml#bapp03-note-0001)) the random variable (*Z* − μ)^TΣ^(− 1)(*Z* − μ) is distributed χ²[*m*]. Thus the ellipsoid centered at *μ*, bounded by a level curve of the density, and containing total probability mass ρ is that given by the equation <displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp03-disp-0003" type="mathematics"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp03\_M0003.gif"><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><msup><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem>

<a href="#bapp03-disp-0003-1">(C.1)</a>![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp03_M0003.gif)

where *k*² is the *ρ*\-quantile of a χ²[*m*] random variable.

## C.1 Parameters to Axes

To compute the axes of the ellipsoid, given *ρ* (and hence *k*) and covariance matrix Σ, let <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp03\_ILM0001.gif"><mrow><mi>&#x039b;</mi><mo>=</mo><mi> diag </mi><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>![](images/bapp03_ILM0001.gif)be the diagonal matrix of eigenvalues of Σ and let Γ be the corresponding matrix of eigenvectors (in columns) so that <displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp03-disp-0004" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp03\_M0004.gif"><mrow><mi>&#x0393;</mi><mi>&#x039b;</mi><mi>&#x0393;</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem>

![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp03_M0004.gif)

Note that Γ is orthonormal, and that all the eigenvalues are positive since Σ is positive definite, so Σ^(− 1) = ΓΛ^(− 1)Γ^T.

Let *w* = Γ^T(*z* − *μ*), so (C.1) is equivalent to <displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp03-disp-0005" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp03\_M0005.gif"><mrow><msup><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mi>&#x0393;</mi><msup><mi>&#x039b;</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>&#x0393;</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>&#x03bc;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>w</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><msup><mi>&#x039b;</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>w</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem>

![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp03_M0005.gif)

The ellipsoid <displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp03-disp-0006" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp03\_M0006.gif"><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>w</mi><mo>:</mo><mi>w</mi><msup><mrow/><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><msup><mi>&#x039b;</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>w</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>}</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem>

![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp03_M0006.gif)

has axes <displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp03-disp-0007" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp03\_M0007.gif"><mrow><mo>{</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>k</mi><msqrt><msub><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msqrt><mo>:</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#x22ef;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>}</mo><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem>

![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp03_M0007.gif)

where *e*[1], …, *e[m]* are the standard basis vectors of <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp03\_ILM0002.gif"><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msup></math>![](images/bapp03_ILM0002.gif). The axes are the columns of matrix <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp03\_ILM0003.gif"><mrow><mi>k</mi><msup><mi>&#x039b;</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup></mrow></math>![](images/bapp03_ILM0003.gif). The volume of the ellipsoid is <displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp03-disp-0008" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp03\_M0008.gif"><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>&#x03c0;</mi><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mrow><mi>&#x0393;</mi><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mfenced></mrow></mfrac><munderover><mo>&#x220f;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></munderover><mi>k</mi><msqrt><msub><mi>&#x03bb;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>&#x03c0;</mi><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mrow><mi>&#x0393;</mi><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mfenced></mrow></mfrac><msup><mi>k</mi><mi>m</mi></msup><msup><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>&#x039b;</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>&#x03c0;</mi><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mrow><mi>&#x0393;</mi><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mfenced></mrow></mfrac><msup><mi>k</mi><mi>m</mi></msup><msup><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem>

![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp03_M0008.gif)

The axes of ellipsoid (C.1) are obtained by transforming back by *z* = Γ*w* + *μ*. They are the columns of <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp03\_ILM0004.gif"><mrow><mi>&#x0393;</mi><mi>k</mi><msup><mi>&#x039b;</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup></mrow></math>![](images/bapp03_ILM0004.gif)(and the ellipsoid is centered at *μ*).

## C.2 Axes to Parameters

To compute the covariance matrix, given *k* and a set of axes {*a*[1], …, *a[m]*}, let Γ be the *m* × *m* matrix whose *i*th column is <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp03\_ILM0005.gif"><mfrac><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mrow><mo>&#x2225;</mo></mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo>&#x2225;</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></math>![](images/bapp03_ILM0005.gif)and let Λ be the *m* × *m* diagonal matrix whose *i*th diagonal element is <math xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" display="inline" location="image\_n/bapp03\_ILM0006.gif"><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo>&#x2225;</mo></mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><msup><mrow><mo>&#x2225;</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><msup><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></math>![](images/bapp03_ILM0006.gif). Then Σ = ΓΛΓ^T. For computational convenience, we note that <displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp03-disp-0009" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp03\_M0009.gif"><mrow><msub><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></munderover><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mspace width="2.em"/><mspace width="-2.0pt"/><msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><munderover><mo>&#x2211;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></munderover><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>&#x2225;</mo></mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><msup><mrow><mo>&#x2225;</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mspace width="2.em"/><mspace width="-2.0pt"/><mi> and </mi><mspace width="2.em"/><mspace width="-2.0pt"/><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>&#x03a3;</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo>&#x220f;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></munderover><msup><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo>&#x2225;</mo></mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mrow><mo>&#x2225;</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></mfrac></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem>

![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp03_M0009.gif)

The volume of the ellipsoid is <displayedItem xmlns:cms="http://cms.wiley.com" xmlns:dctm="http://www.documentum.com" xmlns="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley" xmlns:wiley="http://www.wiley.com/namespaces/wiley/wiley" id="bapp03-disp-0010" type="mathematics" numbered="no"><math display="block" location="image\_n/bapp03\_M0010.gif"><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>&#x03c0;</mi><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mrow><mi>&#x0393;</mi><mfenced separators="" open="(" close=")"><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mfenced></mrow></mfrac><munderover><mo>&#x220f;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></munderover><mrow><mo>&#x2225;</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&#x2225;</mo></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow></math></displayedItem>

![numbered Display Equation](images/bapp03_M0010.gif)
